name: Sakshi Ganapathi Temple
distance: 3 km from Srisailam Temple (on the entry highway)
description: Houses Lord Ganesha who traditionally records the names of all visiting pilgrims to give testimony (Sakshi) to Lord Shiva. Pilgrims traditionally visit this spot first.

name: Paladhara-Panchadhara
distance: 4 km from Srisailam Temple (in a narrow valley)
description: Perennial water streams representing Shiva's five faces. This is the historic site where Sri Adi Shankaracharya meditated and composed his famous Shivananda Lahari.

name: Hatakeswaram
description: An ancient stone temple housing a unique Shiva Lingam where legendary sages performed intensive penance. It plays a significant role in local folklore.

name: Sikharam (Sikhareswara Swamy)
description: The highest geographic point in the Srisailam hills. Features an ancient temple where viewing the main temple's spire through a special column is believed to grant salvation.

name: Pathala Ganga
distance: 1.7 km behind the main Srisailam Temple complex
description: A sacred stretch of the Krishna River down a deep gorge used for holy dips. Accessible via a walk down 600 stone steps or via the APTDC ropeway cable cars.

name: Srisailam Dam & Reservoir View Point
description: Offers panoramic views of the massive dam built across the Krishna River gorge. Features dramatic views during monsoon season when the crest gates are opened.

name: Akkamahadevi Caves
description: Naturally formed dark limestone caves deep in the Nallamala forest. Accessible only via boat ride followed by a short trek to see a self-manifested Shiva Lingam inside.

name: Octopus View Point
description: A deep valley viewpoint offering a bird's-eye perspective of the Krishna River backwaters winding through the hills, creating an appearance resembling an octopus.

name: Chenchu Lakshmi Tribal Museum
description: Managed by the state, this museum displays detailed lifestyle, hunting, and cultural exhibits of the indigenous Chenchu tribes native to the Nallamala forests.
